match.reason: The only candidate, an arithmetic series card from a New South Wales Year 12 course, teaches summing arithmetic sequences, which is a different idea from adding, subtracting and multiplying complex numbers using i² = −1.

draft.title: Arithmetic with complex numbers
card: A complex number has the form a + bi, where a is the real part and b is the imaginary part.
To add or subtract, combine the real parts and the imaginary parts separately. (2 + 3i) + (4 − i) = 6 + 2i.
To multiply, expand like binomials, then replace i² with −1.
draft.remember: Treat i like a pronumeral, then replace i² with −1.

a.why: Subtract the real parts: 5 − 1 = 4. Subtract the imaginary parts: −2 − 4 = −6. The option 4 + 2i comes from not subtracting the sign of the whole bracket.
a.clue: Subtract the whole bracket, including the sign of 4i.

b.why: Expand: 8 − 2i + 12i − 3i² = 8 + 10i + 3 = 11 + 10i. The option 5 + 10i comes from using i² = +1 and getting 8 − 3.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: 4 − 6i and 11 + 10i. The card's examples, the clues and the explanations are all correct.

final.title: Arithmetic with complex numbers
card: A complex number has the form \(a + bi\), where \(a\) is the real part and \(b\) is the imaginary part.
To add or subtract, combine the real parts and the imaginary parts separately. \((2 + 3i) + (4 - i) = 6 + 2i\).
To multiply, expand like binomials, then replace \(i^{2}\) with \(-1\).
final.remember: Treat \(i\) like a pronumeral, then replace \(i^{2}\) with \(-1\).

a.why: Subtract the real parts: \(5 - 1 = 4\). Subtract the imaginary parts: \(-2 - 4 = -6\). The option \(4 + 2i\) comes from not subtracting the sign of the whole bracket.
a.clue: Subtract the whole bracket, including the sign of \(4i\).

b.why: Expand: \(8 - 2i + 12i - 3i^{2} = 8 + 10i + 3 = 11 + 10i\). The option \(5 + 10i\) comes from using \(i^{2} = +1\) and getting \(8 - 3\).
